findings.reason: the earlier review split §14 and §15 for exactly this shape (two deliverables, two independent guards) and both were acted on, so the same rule sends §20 into a code node and a live-graph backfill node.
findings.text: §20 carries two deliverables under one gate: a repository code change (move the `HAS_SUCCESSOR` derivation onto the supersede operation and stop reading the scalar) and a live-graph backfill ("give the 3 names whose only successor pointer is the scalar their edge", measured by a different clause, "the 3 sole-pointer identities resolve their successor through the edge on the live graph"); the code change can pass and the node still fail on live data state it did not create

findings.reason: a worker dispatched on §20 is pointed at `graph_ops.py` for "the supersede operation" that does not exist there, and is not told the write lands in a signed, program-validated mutation, so it can spend its turns in the wrong module or break the signed-program shape.
findings.text: §20's mechanism says to "write the edge … in the operation that marks a name superseded and knows its successor" but names no caller: the only file it cites (`imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py`, ~line 3193) is the derivation being *removed*, whereas the operation that marks a name superseded is the signed `supersede` mutation in `imas_codex/standard_names/signed_manifest.py`, which the cited reader record states ("signed_manifest.py:4712 … mints no edge at all") and flags as the highest-risk decision-needing site in its enumeration
